bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Core idea: systems learn patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trained on labeled data to predict known outputs (e.g., Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with its environment to maximize cumulative rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and adjust internal parameters.
Features and Labels: Features are input variables, labels are target outputs in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for training the model and evaluating its performance.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: Model is too simple, fails to capture important patterns in the data.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicts class probability.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data into subsets based on feature values.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the human brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment recommendations.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Assess performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy, MSE.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate, consistent, and complete data.
Interpretability: Complex models are often difficult to understand, especially in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting a model's ability to generalize.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
ML applications will become more integrated into daily life, enabling smarter technologies.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential as the field progresses.
